directions.title: Active and Semantic SLAM
directions.summary: Meaningful, uncertainty-aware maps for robots that explore on their own.
directions.description: Building meaningful representations of the world for autonomous robots. Our research spans probabilistic semantic mapping and data association, robust visual and RGB-D SLAM in dynamic scenes, Gaussian splatting, and active exploration with UAVs.
directions.hero_text: We build maps that carry meaning and uncertainty, so robots can localize, reason about objects and explore on their own over long missions.

featured.label: Simulation benchmark
featured.title: Bayesian Data Association for Semantic SLAM
featured.text: BPDA-GMM carries association evidence forward with Gaussian mixture models instead of hand-tuned null weights or fixed gates, so semantic landmarks stay consistent under perceptual aliasing.

featured.label: EuRoC benchmark
featured.title: Probabilistically Consistent Visual-Inertial SLAM
featured.text: UC-SLAM builds on ORB-SLAM3 with learned feature uncertainty and a foundation-model metric-depth factor, so features are weighted by content and metric scale does not rely on motion excitation alone.

featured.label: Simulated homes
featured.title: Lifelong Open-Vocabulary Object Maps
featured.text: HiPer learns hierarchical persistence beliefs from data rather than class-based priors, estimating whether each object is still in place after it leaves the robot's view.

featured.label: 7-Scenes
featured.title: Uncertainty-Aware Localization from Gaussian Splatting
featured.text: USGLoc localizes a camera in a semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting map and reports how much to trust the pose, so the estimate can be fused into a Bayesian state estimator.

directions.title: Robust Perception and Autonomous Navigation
directions.summary: Perception that holds up in hard conditions, connected to safe navigation.
directions.description: Perception that keeps working under poor lighting, clutter and sensor noise, connected to safe decisions. We work on illumination-robust visual front-ends, multisensor fusion for localization and obstacle avoidance, semantic-aware path planning for UAVs, swarms of drones and robots that navigate together, and social navigation with motion prediction around people.
directions.hero_text: We make perception hold up under poor light, clutter and sensor noise, and connect it to safe navigation for UAVs and mobile robots.

featured.label: Method overview
featured.title: Illumination-Robust Visual SLAM Front-End
featured.text: IRAF-SLAM enhances images under changing light and adapts feature culling, keeping visual SLAM tracking stable through sudden lighting changes, low texture and dynamic objects.

featured.label: UAV perception
featured.title: Semantic-Aware Path Planning for Reliable UAV Localization
featured.text: Real-time semantic segmentation from a monocular camera guides the UAV around texture-less areas such as lakes and high-rise buildings, where localization would otherwise fail.

featured.label: Method overview
featured.title: Social Navigation with Motion Prediction
featured.text: Human trajectory prediction is folded into Timed Elastic Band planning with social constraints, so a service robot moves safely and politely around people.

featured.label: Real-world demo
featured.title: Multisensor Fusion for Obstacle Avoidance
featured.text: Two depth cameras and a LiDAR are fused into one view around the robot, and a dynamic-window planner uses it to avoid obstacles in real corridors.

directions.title: Robot Learning and Human–Robot Interaction
directions.summary: Robots that learn from demonstrations and work naturally with people.
directions.description: Learning robot behavior from demonstrations, video and interaction. We study imitation learning from human video, reinforcement learning with stable policy optimization, object-centric video understanding for manipulation commands, and humanoid interaction through gestures, speech and language models.
directions.hero_text: We teach robots from human demonstrations and interaction, and build humanoid and manipulation systems that work naturally with people.

featured.label: Real-robot demo
featured.title: From Video Demonstrations to Robot Commands
featured.text: Object-centric video understanding separates action recognition from object grounding, turning human demonstration videos into robot commands that name the right objects.

featured.label: Humanoid simulation
featured.title: Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures for Humanoids
featured.text: A language model splits dialogue into semantic gesture units, and constrained wavefront optimization keeps the humanoid's gestures in time with speech within its joint and actuator limits.

featured.label: Grasp reasoning
featured.title: Calibrated Obstruction Reasoning for Grasping in Clutter
featured.text: Calibrated vision-language predictions and probabilistic reasoning over alternative obstruction graphs decide whether to grasp the target, remove a blocker, or wait.

featured.label: Real-world demo
featured.title: Dual-Arm Service Robot for Human–Robot Interaction
featured.text: Design, fabrication and structural optimization of a mobile dual-arm service robot built for navigation, manipulation and interaction with people.

directions.title: Agentic Robotics and Industrial Vision
directions.summary: Robots that plan and coordinate as agents, and vision for industrial inspection.
directions.description: Robots that plan, schedule and coordinate tasks as agents, and vision systems for industry. Work includes online scheduling for multi-robot collaboration, monocular 3D object localization for industrial robot vision, and super-resolution methods for detecting tiny defects on printed circuit boards.
directions.hero_text: We build robots that plan and coordinate tasks as agents with humans and other robots, and vision systems for industrial inspection.

featured.label: Human–robot collaboration
featured.title: Online Scheduling for Multi-Robot Collaboration
featured.text: A language model plans long-horizon tasks as a dependency graph, and an online scheduler runs them in parallel across heterogeneous robots and people.

featured.label: Preprint
featured.title: Agentic Humanoid Robots for Industrial Safety
featured.text: A ReAct-style agent on a Unitree G1 humanoid combines RGB-D perception and learned locomotion to detect fire and smoke, abnormal pipeline temperatures and intruders in unmanned factories.

featured.label: Method overview
featured.title: Tiny PCB Defect Detection
featured.text: Edge-guided super-resolution and ensemble learning recover detail in low-resolution images of printed circuit boards, separating tiny defects from noise.

featured.label: Method overview
featured.title: Monocular 3D Localization for Industrial Robot Vision
featured.text: Object detection, post-processing and 3D calibration locate flat parts from a single 2D image, for low-cost industrial robot cells.

research_interests: We are also interested in lifelong SLAM, robot dynamics learning, model-based reinforcement learning and learning from demonstration. Modeling uncertainty in map representations and robot dynamics is central to our interests in safe, active planning and control.

members.name: Thanh Nguyen Canh
members.bio: Thanh Nguyen Canh is a lecturer in the Robotics Department at the University of Engineering and Technology, Vietnam National University (VNU-UET), and a Ph.D. candidate at the Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (JAIST), working on 3D active semantic SLAM, robot perception, navigation and learning.

focus.title: Robot Autonomy
paragraphs: Robot autonomy means machines that perceive their surroundings, build and keep maps of the world, and decide how to act without constant human guidance.

PAIRS Lab builds the perception, mapping and learning that autonomous robots need outside the lab: maps that carry meaning and uncertainty, perception that holds up in hard conditions, robots that learn from people, and agents that plan and coordinate tasks. We test our methods on aerial robots, mobile robots, manipulators and humanoids.
